tools.detail: TensorFlow is an open-source machine learning framework developed by Google Brain team. It is designed to be flexible and efficient for a wide range of tasks, from basic data analysis to complex deep learning models. Key features include support for both CPU and GPU acceleration, a flexible architecture for defining computational graphs, and a wide range of pre-trained models. TensorFlow is suitable for researchers, data scientists, and developers looking to build and deploy machine learning models. Pros include its scalability, robustness, and extensive community support. Limitations may include a steep learning curve and a more complex setup process for beginners.

tools.detail: PyTorch is an open-source machine learning library based on the Torch library, developed by Facebook's AI Research lab. Key features include automatic differentiation, support for both CPU and GPU, and a wide range of pre-trained models. PyTorch is ideal for researchers and developers who want to prototype and experiment with machine learning models quickly. Pros include its intuitive interface and flexibility. tools.name: BERT
tools.desc: Pre-trained language representation for natural language understanding
pros: Free and open source, transparent code, self-hostable for full data control
Supports local / Docker deployment, better data privacy
Free version available, zero cost for personal use
cons: Requires some technical skill to deploy and configure
usage:
Step: Check your environment
This tool runs locally. First make sure your computer meets the basics.
Tip:
Install the required runtime (see README).
Check:
Open a terminal and type `the command`. If you see a version number, your environment is OK.

Step: Download the code to your machine
Open a terminal in a folder you like and run the commands below:
Code:
git clone https://github.com/google-research/bert.git
cd bert
Tip:
New to git? If it says command not found, download it from https://git-scm.com.

Step: Install dependencies
The project needs some extra building blocks to run.
Code:
make install
Tip:
If a command errors, it is usually a network issue. Python users can try a mirror.

Step: Fill in the API Key / account config
Many AI tools need a model connection. Find the config item in the README and fill it in.
Code:
# Example: replace xxx with your real Key
export OPENAI_API_KEY="sk-xxx"
Tip:
Do not screenshot your Key in public groups. Get a free/cheap Key (e.g. GLM-4, DeepSeek) to practice.

Step: Start and run your first task
Run the example command from the project and watch the terminal output.
Code:
./run.sh
Check:
If the program prints results (no red Error text), you have it working.

Step: Troubleshooting
Failing the first local deploy is normal. Common issues:
1. Dependency version mismatch → use the Python/Node version the repo recommends;
2. Key not working → check your environment variables;
3. Cannot reach the model API → switch mirror or provider.
Tip:
See more examples in "Related tutorials" below, or click "Visit official site".
tools.detail: BERT (Bidirectional Encoder Representations from Transformers) is a pre-trained language representation model developed by Google. It is designed to understand the context of words in a sentence, making it highly effective for various NLP tasks. Key features include its ability to pre-train on a large corpus of text and fine-tune on specific tasks, and its support for both token-level and sentence-level representations. BERT is suitable for researchers, developers, and data scientists working on NLP tasks. Pros include its strong performance on a wide range of NLP tasks and its ease of integration into existing systems. Limitations may include the need for significant computational resources for training and the complexity of fine-tuning for specific tasks.

tools.detail: Prophet is an open-source tool designed to forecast time series data. It is particularly effective for data that has strong seasonal effects and several cycles per year. Key features of Prophet include automatic handling of daily, weekly, and yearly seasonality, as well as the ability to model multiple yearly seasonality patterns. It is designed to be easy to use and extend, with a Python interface and a wide range of customization options. Prophet is suitable for a variety of applications, such as demand forecasting, inventory planning, and financial analysis. It is widely used in data science and business intelligence teams. Pros of Prophet include its robustness in handling complex time series data and its user-friendly interface. Limitations include the need for a significant amount of historical data to accurately forecast future trends and the complexity of setting up and tuning the model for optimal performance.
